column1: # Targets of the function-pointer dispatch sites on the x86_64 interrupt path.
# The walker follows direct call edges only, so without this file it stops at
# the first `call *%rax` and reports the receive path as 8 bytes deep. Every
# hardware interrupt handler here is reached through a registered `fn` pointer:
# the MSI vector table, the x86 line-handler table, the nine softirq slots, the
# tick-poll hook and the exit-to-user hook. Each has a handful of registration
# sites, all in this tree, so the target sets are finite and nameable.
# Format: `<caller>\t<callee>`, demangled identities, caller repeated per
# target. An entry that no longer resolves FAILS the gate — a map that has
# drifted silently restores the blindness it exists to remove.
# NAPI poll list, one level BELOW the softirq table: `net_rx_action` walks the
# inlined into it, so the edge is attributed to `net_rx_action` itself. Missing
# this edge understated the interrupt domain by the whole receive path.
